section.t: To ensure absolute transparency, prevent unmanaged out-of-band disclosures, and safeguard the consensus-finding process, the IETF Datatracker MUST structurally enforce deterministic system states. These granular states establish an unalterable, verifiable ledger of all procedural milestones by consolidating and cleaning up all traditional evaluation steps into a single, linear process symmetry as detailed in the following table. Technical content modifications MUST be programmatically prohibited immediately upon a document transitioning into State 4 and during all subsequent states.

tr.td: Free submission of technological ideas from the ground (Bottom-Up).
Official adoption by the WG. System-enforced timeouts start.
Requires formal WG Adoption Consensus. Automation triggers strict 90-day review limit.
Technological core is frozen. No asymmetric late changes allowed.
Requires formal Working Group Last Call (WGLC) completion. Last chance for technical changes.
The entire Area must document consensus for IESG submission. No AD individual veto.
Requires documented Area-wide consensus. Technical content changing is prohibited. Only editorial fixes.
Last Call and global validation of interoperability. Static review only.
Requires completion of IETF-wide Last Call. Static validation only; any technical error forces drop to Level 1.
Automated, machine-driven RFC minting. AUTH48 is strict syntax-check only.
Automated trigger by RFC Editor. Maximum 14-day timeout. Absolute freeze of both content and layout.

section.t: On complex and possibly difficult to consider topics according to the IESG MAY consider consultig the IAB. However, in the event of collevtive recusal the duty of the IESG is to forward the document to the IAB.
If no fitting Working Group exists, the responsible Area Review Team or Directorate is requested to perform Early and Final Reviews.

Any kind of Process Variance requires the explicit authorization of the IESG or, if requested by it, of the IAB. A process variance can only be granted upon an exact description of it and its requirements.

li.t: On State 1 -> 2 transition the Working Group has full control of the document, if the draft author is not the appointed editor.
On State 2 -> 3 transition the 14-day Working Group Last Call SHALL be immidiately initiated.
On transition, the responsible Area Director is requested to perform a pre-Area Last Call Review and to initiate an Area Last Call subsequently.
Drafts coming from State 1 will be injected here directly, bypassing the Working Group states.
On reachin Area Consensus this document SHALL be immidiately forwarded to the IESG. Which is REQUIRED to initiate:
a immidiate pre IETF Last Call Review, which MUST NOT be done by the Area Director who has done the pre Area Last Call Review, a external entity SHALL be prefered.
Subsequently to this review a immidiate IETF Last Call MUST take place within five business days.
Upon reaching IETF consensus, the IESG is REQUIRED to forward the document in consent to the RFC Production Center immidiately.
